transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-04-22 11:00 AM PT / 19:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Ramos (Redwood AE), Priya Mehta (Redwood SE), Mark Bennett (Meridian - Security Lead), Clara Ortiz (Meridian - Platform), Sasha Cole (Meridian - Compliance)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on security/compliance gating items: SSO test, audit log samples and retention window, SOC2 artifacts and where Redwood fits for encryption and key management. Agreed on action items: Redwood to send a consolidated security package and SOC2 checklist, SE to stand up an SSO test tenant and share SAML metadata, Meridian to confirm retention windows and event list. Agreed to a live audit-logs demo next week.

Topics discussed: SSO / SAML onboarding, audit log schema and export, data retention policy and legal export, SOC2 evidence mapping, KMS/Key rotation, RBAC scoping for pilot users.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Ramos: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're about 50 minutes allocated, uh we want to run through the security checklist and make sure the pilot isn't blocked by any compliance asks. Mark, Sasha, you good with that agenda?
[00:08] Mark Bennett: Yeah that's fine. Sorry, I'm on mobile, connection a bit spotty, but—yes that's fine.
[00:12] Sasha Cole: All good here. Would love to nail down retention numbers.
[00:15] Priya Mehta: Great, quick intro from the SE side, I'm Priya, I'll be setting up the SAML test tenant and we can demo the audit logs schema.
[00:22] Clara Ortiz: Quick housekeeping — our infra folks care about key rotation and HSM support, that's high priority.
[00:27] Alex Ramos: Noted. Okay start with SSO. Priya, status?
[00:30] Priya Mehta: We stood up a sandbox tenant yesterday and I have a SAML metadata blob, but I haven't shared it yet. I can export the metadata and the IdP config. There's the usual gotchas — NameID format, Attribute statements. In our hosted product we support SAML 2.0, SSO via SAML or OIDC. For the private deployment we can also do a customer-managed IdP.
[00:50] Mark Bennett: For Meridian we need SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning — we want accounts auto-provisioned and de-provisioned. Also need to map group claims to RBAC roles.
[01:02] Priya Mehta: SCIM is supported in the Dedicated and Private pilots; for hosted we can enable a SCIM endpoint for the tenant. There's a small step to wire in the SCIM tokens. We'll share a sample user mapping table.
[01:16] Mark Bennett: Cool. Also, MFA required for admin roles — we need to know how that hooks into your RBAC.
[01:22] Alex Ramos: MFA enforced by the IdP is fine for us; RBAC within Redwood maps groups to roles. We'll provide docs and an example mapping.
[01:30] Clara Ortiz: Next, audit logs: we need a sample of events, schema, and retention behaviour. Are logs immutable? Can we export to our SIEM?
[01:40] Priya Mehta: Yes — logs are append-only in our system and we stream audit events to S3 or a customer syslog/HTTPS endpoint. For the pilot we'll provide a daily export and a live stream demo. The event schema includes user, action, resource, timestamp, request id, and the high-level model invocation metadata. The transcript or request payloads by default are not included unless you enable full request logging — which we can toggle.
[02:04] Sasha Cole: That's key because PII in requests — we cannot keep full request bodies for more than 30 days in our environment. What's the retention config for both hosted and private?
[02:15] Priya Mehta: For hosted, default retention for request bodies is 30 days, audit metadata 365 days, but these are tunable. For Dedicated we can set policy per tenant, and for Private you control the storage backend and retention. We'll show the config UI and the config-as-code options.
[02:34] Mark Bennett: Are there redaction options? We need automatic PII redaction for names and ssn-like patterns.
[02:40] Priya Mehta: There's a configurable redaction pipeline — regex-based and ML-assisted PII detection. It's part of Redwood Optimize; for the pilot we'll enable a rule set and show a before/after sample. Note transcription sometimes shows weird capitalization or mis-heard words — so ML redaction needs some tuning.
[02:58] Alex Ramos: (laughs) yeah the transcript is never perfect.
[03:00] Mark Bennett: About SOC 2 — we need a mapping of your SOC 2 controls to our assessment checklist. Do you have an artifact bundle we can review?
[03:09] Alex Ramos: Yes, we'll send a security package: SOC 2 type II summary, control narratives, encryption diagrams, key management notes and a list of third-party sub processors. Expect that in an email from me by Thursday 4/24.
[03:20] Sasha Cole: Are you encrypting data at rest with customer keys? We prefer CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys).
[03:27] Priya Mehta: We support CMEK for Dedicated and for Private deployments; hosted can be integrated with KMS via a customer-managed key in supported cloud providers. Key rotation is supported and we maintain key usage logs. We can show key rotation workflows.
[03:42] Clara Ortiz: Important: our auditors will want to see proof of key rotation and key destruction procedures.
[03:47] Alex Ramos: We'll add rotation docs and the HSM bit to the package.
[03:50] Mark Bennett: Another question: can audit logs be exported in near-real time to our Splunk? We don't want to pull batches.
[03:59] Priya Mehta: Yes, we can stream to Kinesis/CloudWatch/Splunk HTTP Event Collector. For the POC we can demo Splunk HEC; it's a configuration toggle and a small connector.
[04:10] Sasha Cole: One caveat — retention for exported logs is in our control, but the system's internal retention must still respect policy. So we need assurance that exported logs are not the only copy.
[04:20] Priya Mehta: Understood — exported copies are separate; internal platform copies honor the tenant retention policy. We'll provide a diagram showing the lifecycle.
[04:28] Alex Ramos: Let's talk about evidence for SOC2: what's the minimum artifact set you need? Sasha?
[04:33] Sasha Cole: We'll need admin access logs, change control tickets for releases that touched infra, encryption key rotation records, SOC2 report, and vendor/subprocessor list. Ideally something that maps each control to an artifact.
[04:44] Alex Ramos: We'll produce a control matrix mapping Redwood controls to your audit points.
[04:48] Mark Bennett: Another operational concern — service accounts and least privilege. How granular is RBAC? Can we create a read-only observer role for compliance folks?
[04:58] Priya Mehta: Yes, roles are highly configurable. You can create scoped roles — e.g., read-only for logs, or model-deploy-only for platform teams. We'll send sample role YAMLs.
[05:08] Clara Ortiz: For the Dedicated pilot we want to pin model versions and disable auto-updates, to reduce variance while auditors review. Is that possible?
[05:16] Alex Ramos: Yes, pinning and canary rollouts are supported. For the pilot we can pin to a specific model commit and disable auto-updates. We'll note that in playbook.
[05:23] Mark Bennett: One more: data residency and data egress. Some PHI-related tests require logs to stay in-region. Does Redwood offer region pinning?
[05:33] Priya Mehta: Yes, region pinning is part of Dedicated and Private; hosted tenants can be assigned to region-specific clusters in many cases. We'll include region mapping and network egress controls in the docs.
[05:45] Alex Ramos: Ok, let's move to next steps and timing. We want an audit-logs demo — live streaming and a small query/grep demo where Clara's team can run queries for a given request id. Priya, can you set that up?
[05:56] Priya Mehta: Yep, I'll schedule a 45-minute walkthrough for the week of 4/28, and include a Splunk HEC config example. I'll also drop the SAML metadata and SCIM instructions ahead of time.
[06:06] Mark Bennett: We'll collate a list of required events and sample PII patterns (emails, MRNs) and share by 4/28.
[06:14] Sasha Cole: We also need an export template for legal — CSV with specific columns for retention audits.
[06:20] Priya Mehta: We have a premade export template, will attach to the security package.
[06:25] Alex Ramos: Any blockers or open questions?
[06:27] Mark Bennett: Only to make sure the PII redaction works on the kinds of messages we have in our prompts — we sometimes include patient initials. We want to test ML-assisted redaction versus pattern-only.
[06:37] Priya Mehta: We'll enable both and show side-by-side. Also will surface false-positive tuning knobs.
[06:43] Clara Ortiz: Technical note: our SIEM team will provide a test token for Splunk; I'll share that in a separate email.
[06:48] Alex Ramos: Good. Last, schedule and deliverables recap. I'll email the security bundle and SOC2 mapping by 4/24. Priya will stand up SSO sandbox and share SAML + SCIM by 4/25. We'll schedule the audit-logs demo week of 4/28. Meridian to provide retention policy and event list by 4/28.
[07:05] Sasha Cole: Sounds good.
[07:07] Mark Bennett: Thanks everyone.
[07:09] Alex Ramos: Thanks — we'll follow up in writing and update the CRM. Bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional words may be mis-heard (e.g., HSM heard as "H S M"), speaker overlaps with brief crosstalk. References to product internals like KV cache or request prefix cache showed up but were not central to this call.
